timeouts._comment: Downstream (Prefill/Decode) HTTP timeout. A stalled KV handoff would otherwise leave the router handler and its inflight counters hung forever, wedging every later request; the handler now fails the request instead.

a100._address_comment: 2026-09-13: canonical address is 10.66.0.15:2222 (overlay path). 10.70.251.47 is the same host (identical SSH host key, same ray node) reached over the older direct route, and is no longer used by any tooling. prefills._comment: A100 node is a shared machine; other users can reclaim the GPUs and remove foreign containers at any time. 2026-09-13: node was free, so the instance is enabled. speed/capacity/service_ms were declared while only two of eight GPUs were available, so they must be re-measured on the free node before quoting them.

decodes._comment: A100 node is a shared machine; other users can reclaim the GPUs and remove foreign containers at any time. 2026-09-13: node was free, so the instance is enabled. speed/capacity/service_ms were declared while only two of eight GPUs were available, so they must be re-measured on the free node before quoting them.

weights._chars_per_token_comment: Seed only (was 6.7): the router fits the ratio from the engine's own usage.prompt_tokens and converged on 4.46 within 12 requests of real traffic (2026-09-14). The old 6.7 under-stated every token count by ~1.5x, and with it every KV byte the link budget is denominated in.

casr._comment: Mirrors the simulator cluster 'casr' block. Capacity is the measured engine throughput (max_num_seqs*1000/service_ms); compute_weight prices per-request service time scaled by the prefix-cache miss ratio, and utilization_weight adds the convex congestion price that stops the LP from stacking every class on one P/D pair.

structural._comment: Economics of a structural edit, calibrated 2026-09-14. evaluation_window_ms is the horizon the edit must repay within (the expected overload duration, not one control tick): with 1 s, no real container start-up can ever be repaid, so the decision degenerated to 'a stopped spare exists -> start it' (measured: +P fired at tick 0 on a nearly idle pool with gain 0.0375, while the same counterfactual at the real peak is worth ~10/s). startup_s is the measured WARMING time of a restarted container (45 s on 2026-09-13/14); the +P gain only accrues over horizon - startup_s, and it also becomes the minimum cooldown so a decision is not reversed inside its own boot. idle_cost_fraction charges each active Prefill 10% of its saturated compute cost per second, which is what makes -P able to win: with no holding cost every -P counterfactual was mechanically negative and the pool could only ever grow. max_active_prefill caps scale-out; 0/absent means 'every configured Prefill'.

casr._slo_comment: Application-level interactive bound: TTFT <= 500 ms and TPOT <= 50 ms (see docs/实验数据集与对比基线说明.md).  A (class, prefill, decode) triple whose predicted TTFT exceeds ttft_slo_ms gets +slo_penalty on its unit cost, so the LP avoids it while a capacity shortfall still yields a plan.  SLO_TTFT_MS / SLO_PENALTY env vars override these at run time for sweeps.
casr._ttft_model_comment: Fixed TTFT-path overheads measured on 2026-09-12 from /tmp/casr-md/lp43-r{1,2}: prefill_overhead = router-observed prefill_ms - service_ms (p50: p5090 101-48.5, p3090a 252-68, p4090 112.5-39.2); decode_ttft = ttft_ms - prefill_ms (p50: d5090/d4090 56 ms, d3090a scaled by its service ratio 421.6/144.7).  Without these the predicted TTFT of an idle cluster is ~50 ms against a real ~240 ms, so no realistic SLO ever binds.

casr._decode_capacity_comment: Measured saturation throughput (req/s) from tests/calibrate_pd_throughput.py at a 2048-token prefix / 4 output tokens: d5090 60-70, d3090a 23-29, d4090 53-57. The derived max_num_seqs*1000/service_ms overestimates by ~2x because engine throughput does not scale linearly with batch size.
casr._warmup_comment: Plan policies only, disabled by default.  The mechanism is functional (the serving edge is now recorded as warm, earlier it never was -- see docs/异构环境搭建进展.md 'casr_lp 尾部调查'), but enabling it did not move the 2026-09-13 saturation tail, so the default stays off.
casr._single_home_comment: lp27 A/B: a class offering < 1 req/s is single-homed onto the Prefill the LP liked best, unless that would overflow the Prefill or its KV-push link. Targets the +74 cold first-touches the LP created by splitting low-demand classes across Prefills.
casr._capacity_comment: prefill_capacity is the MEASURED saturation point tests/calibrate_pd_throughput.py 2026-09-13 (1024-token prefix, 4 output tokens, 32 reqs/level): p5090=62.9, p4090=58.5 req/s. The previous values (330/408) were declared from max_num_seqs*1000/service_ms and overstate the knee 5-7x, so the LP never saw the load pressure it should. p3090a/p3090b/p_a100 are unmeasured and are scaled from the declared hardware ratio; p_a100 became reachable and idle on 2026-09-13, so it can now be calibrated with tests/calibrate_pd_throughput.py before its capacity is quoted.
casr._kv_cost_comment: Native NixlConnector handoff cost measured 2026-09-13 (tests/calibrate_native_pd.py, unique prompt per sample): p5090->d5090 (same host) 163 ms + 585 ms/1k tokens; p5090->d4090 211 ms + 1351 ms/1k tokens; p5090->d3090a 415 ms + 1364 ms/1k tokens. For comparison the Decode recomputing the same prompt locally costs ~93 ms. A handoff is therefore 8-15x MORE expensive than recomputing, so the scheduler must treat 'transfer' as a resource it spends only when the alternative (Decode-side prefill / queueing) is worse -- the current pair-cost model still assumes a transfer always happens. A100 domain (now on vLLM 0.29 and inside the NIXL fabric): p_a100->d5090 544 ms + 8223 ms/1k (18.3 MB/s); p5090->d_a100 626 ms + 10163 ms/1k (14.8 MB/s). That is a 14x spread against the same-host 257 MB/s, i.e. the heterogeneous link the scheduler has to price.
casr._prefill_speed_comment: Measured local prefill cost 2026-09-13 (TTFT of a ~850-token prompt sent directly to the instance, 3 samples, median; includes the network RTT to the instance): d5090 50.9, d4090 64.6, d3090a 156.1, d_a100 202.4 ms/1k tokens. Relative to the 5090 that is 1.00 / 0.79 / 0.33 / 0.30 (sharing the a100 node's GPU makes it the slowest, not the fastest as the earlier declared speed=2.0 assumed).
casr._decode_capacity_comment_measured: Decode service capacity re-based on a measured concurrency sweep 2026-09-13 (12 concurrent ~180-token prompts, 16 output tokens, single instance): d5090 40.5, d4090 33.7, d_a100 23.8, d3090a 15.9 req/s. Values here keep d5090's declared scale and apply the measured ratios, so the fast layer's inflight/capacity ranking reflects reality instead of the declared hardware ratios (which had made the A100 look like the strongest decode).
casr._prefill_capacity_comment_measured: Prefill capacity re-based on a measured concurrency sweep 2026-09-13 (12 concurrent ~180-token prompts, max_tokens=1, single instance): p5090 156.2, p4090 162.0, p3090a 80.7, p3090b 61.7, p_a100 51.3 req/s. The declared a100 value (550) was 10.7x its measured rate and made the least-loaded baseline pile 95% of prefills onto the slowest node; these values keep p5090's declared scale and apply the measured ratios.
casr._length_comment: Pre-2026-09-14 the LP scaled nothing by length: a 1250-token request cost the same as a 200-token one, so prefill_overflow stayed 0 on a node whose queue was 48 deep. prefill_tokens_per_s is the measured token ceiling; decode_* model the decode leg's output-length cost (20 ms fixed + 14 ms/token, calibrated on d5090's 226 ms for 16 output tokens).
casr._backlog_comment: Demand recovered from Prefill queue growth: the arrival EWMA alone is post-backpressure, so under overload demand reads as == capacity. Caps the added term at this multiple of the observed arrival rate.
casr._prefill_tokens_comment: Measured 2026-09-14, unique prefixes, prefill-only, concurrency 16: p5090 11.3 req/s @1250 tokens / 71.9 @254 (14.1-18.3 ktok/s, take the conservative 14.1k), p4090 8.4 / 40.8 (10.4 ktok/s, flat). p3090a/b/p_a100 were not measured; scaled from p5090 by their declared capacity ratio. The declared prefill_capacity is only valid below tokens = ceiling/capacity.
